# Policy Model and Expressiveness

Dimension covering YAML policy syntax, what can and cannot be controlled,
granularity, policy composition, and developer workflow.

## Policy Structure

Top-level YAML with four sections [3]:

```yaml
version: 1              # Must be 1
filesystem_policy: {}   # Static — locked at creation
landlock: {}            # Static — locked at creation
process: {}             # Static — locked at creation
network_policies: {}    # Dynamic — hot-reloadable
```

"Static sections are locked at sandbox creation. Changing them requires
destroying and recreating the sandbox" [5].

## Filesystem Policy (Static)

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `include_workdir` | bool | Auto-adds agent's working directory to `read_write` [3] |
| `read_only` | string list | Readable but unmodifiable paths [3] |
| `read_write` | string list | Readable and writable paths [3] |

Unlisted paths are inaccessible — **deny-by-default** [3].

### Validation Constraints

- Paths must be absolute (start with `/`) [3]
- No `..` traversal components [3]
- Read-write paths cannot be overly broad (e.g., `/` rejected) [3]
- Maximum 4096 characters per path [3]
- Combined total of 256 paths maximum [3]
- Violations trigger `INVALID_ARGUMENT` rejection [3]

## Landlock (Static)

| Field | Type | Values |
|-------|------|--------|
| `compatibility` | string | `best_effort` or `hard_requirement` [3][5] |

`best_effort` uses highest available kernel ABI; `hard_requirement` fails if
Landlock is unavailable [5].

## Process (Static)

| Field | Type | Default |
|-------|------|---------|
| `run_as_user` | string | `sandbox` [3] |
| `run_as_group` | string | `sandbox` [3] |

"Neither field accepts root or 0 values" [3].

## Network Policies (Dynamic)

Map of named entries controlling which binaries reach which endpoints [3].

### Endpoint Object

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `host` | string | Hostname/IP; supports `*.example.com` wildcards [3] |
| `port` | integer | TCP port [3] |
| `protocol` | string | `rest` for HTTP inspection; omit for TCP passthrough [3] |
| `enforcement` | string | `enforce` or `audit` (logs only) [3] |
| `access` | string | `full`, `read-only`, `read-write` [3] |
| `rules` | list | Fine-grained per-method/path rules (mutually exclusive with `access`) [3] |

### Access Levels (L7)

| Level | HTTP Methods |
|-------|-------------|
| `full` | All methods and paths [3] |
| `read-only` | GET, HEAD, OPTIONS [3] |
| `read-write` | GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST, PUT, PATCH [3] |

### Fine-Grained Rules

- `allow.method`: HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) [3]
- `allow.path`: URL path pattern with `*` and `**` glob support [3]

### Binary Object

- `path`: Filesystem path with `*` and `**` glob patterns [3]

## Inference Routing

`inference.local` endpoint exposed inside every sandbox [7]:

1. "Strips original credentials from sandbox requests" [7]
2. "Injects configured backend credentials before forwarding" [7]

- Single provider-model pairing per gateway [7]
- Hot-refresh: ~5 seconds propagation [7]
- Supported: NVIDIA, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible providers [7]
- "Requests not matching configured provider's patterns are denied" [7]

## Policy Workflow

### Applying Policies

```bash
openshell sandbox create --policy ./my-policy.yaml -- claude
# or via environment variable:
export OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_POLICY=./my-policy.yaml
```
[5]

### Hot-Reload (Network Policies Only)

Six-step iterative cycle [5]:

1. Create sandbox with initial policy
2. Monitor logs: `openshell logs <name> --tail --source sandbox`
3. Pull current: `openshell policy get <name> --full > current-policy.yaml`
4. Edit YAML
5. Push: `openshell policy set <name> --policy current-policy.yaml --wait`
6. Verify: `openshell policy list <name>`

### Global Override

`openshell policy set --global --policy ./global-policy.yaml` — "When global
policies active, individual sandbox-level updates rejected" [5].

## Agent Compatibility

| Agent | Default Policy Coverage | Notes |
|-------|------------------------|-------|
| Claude Code | Full | Works out-of-box [4] |
| OpenCode | Partial | Requires additional endpoint configuration [4] |
| Codex | None | Requires custom policy [4] |

"If you run a non-Claude agent without a custom policy, the agent's API calls
are denied by the proxy" [4].

## What CAN Be Controlled

- Filesystem read/write per-path with Landlock kernel enforcement [3]
- Network egress per-binary, per-host, per-port at L4; per-method/path at L7 [3]
- Process identity (non-root user/group) [3]
- Syscall filtering via seccomp [5]
- Inference routing destination and credential injection [7]
- Audit mode vs enforce mode per endpoint [3]
- Global policy override locking out per-sandbox changes [5]

## What CANNOT Be Controlled

- No per-file granularity — directory-level paths only [3]
- No write-only paths (only read_only and read_write) [3]
- No time-based or rate-limiting policies
- No content inspection beyond HTTP method/path (no request body filtering) [3]
- No per-user or per-role policies within a sandbox [3]
- No DNS-level filtering
- No UDP or non-TCP protocol policies
- Network policies are egress-only
- Inference routing is per-gateway, not per-sandbox [7]

## Gaps and Limitations

- Policy schema version is `1` with no stability guarantees documented [3]
- The 256-path limit may incentivize overly broad path specifications [3]
- `audit` enforcement mode logs but does not block — easy to forget [3]
- Config file protection requires explicit policy configuration; not in defaults [4]
